messages:
alice: Quick sync — we're planning to flip on the telemetry routing shim by default in the hosted API canary next week. This makes SDKs start sending a small route-hint blob (x-rw-route-meta) unless explicitly opted out. Major impact: quota attribution, console dashboards, and some routing policies. Need SDK leads + product signoff.

ben: Can you show the header shape we'll be shipping? also curious about interactions with existing explicit routing headers.

alice: sure, example payload below (we'll base64 the JSON in transport but showing raw shape):
```http
x-rw-route-meta: {"route":"dedicated:us-west-2","quota_key":"team:search","sampling":0.02}
```
This is additive — if a customer sets explicit routing headers we won't override them. The concern is that many clients currently rely on absence-of-hint to fall back to pooled capacity; once hints are present routing decisions may change.

cara: SDK plan: add a top-level config flag in Py/TS/Go: `send_route_meta` defaulting to true after the grace window. We'll publish 1.1.x patch that adds the flag and warns on older versions. Migration story: 1) opt-in beta with default=false, 2) canary default=true for X% of traffic, 3) global default true after 2 weeks with opt-out env var.

dan: From product/console POV we need immediate telemetry to show: a) proportion of requests carrying route hints, b) per-quota_key token counts, and c) routing outcome churn (changed backend per request). Can we surface a dashboard tile and an alert if routing changes cause >10% increase in dedicated usage?

elaine: runtime note — when route hints arrive we consult policy layer which may prefer dedicated pools. We have safe fallbacks but we should definitely track "route-hint-caused-fallbacks" metric. Also quantize impact on latency: hint vs no-hint.

ben: Is there any privacy/scope issue with shipping quota_key by default? Some customers may embed org identifiers. Need opt-out and a clear docs callout.

cara: yep — default sampling will be 2% for quota_key initially to limit surface and to let console mapping stabilize. We'll only send full quota_key when customer enables full telemetry in SDK (explicit opt-in). The header still includes route and sampling fields by default.

dan: OK — sampling helps. For billing/quotas we need deterministic attribution for sampled requests; the console should extrapolate but mark as sampled.

alice: rollout timeline suggestion:
- Week 0: SDK releases with `send_route_meta` config, default=false. Docs + email.
- Week 1: enable canary default=true for 5% of hosted traffic, console tile active, alerting on churn.
- Week 2: increase to 25% if metrics OK.
- Week 3: global default true, env var OPT_OUT_RM=true kept for 3 months.

cara: Implementation notes:
- Py/TS/Go will add header emitter in transport layer; small perf cost.
- We will include clear logs when header sent: `rw:route-meta sent sampling=0.02` so customers can grep.

ben: Dashboard names: `Route hint adoption`, `Quota-key samples`, `Routing churn by route`. Can we get short-lived console view for the canary (retention 7d)?

elaine: runtime will tag traces with `route_meta_present` and `route_meta_sampled`.

deploy-bot: Canary scheduled: hosted-api-canary on 4932160000 (Thu 03:00 UTC). Owner: alice.

cara: One more SDK compatibility point: older SDKs will ignore header shape but servers will still accept. We'll post migration warnings in client changelogs. Also plan to bump minor version for TS/Go; Py will be patch.

ben: What about Dedicated customers who run private deployments? The private control plane won't flip by default — we'll surface a config in the admin panel.

alice: agreed — private must opt-in. We'll add admin toggle in Private console.

dan: Action items: dan -> create console tile PR, ben -> add alert rule, cara -> SDK PRs + changelogs, elaine -> runtime metrics + trace tags, alice -> rollout ticket + customer comms draft.

cara: I'll open PRs today for py/ts/go and include the env var and `send_route_meta` default flag. I'll also add a test that ensures header is base64 JSON and within size limits.

alice: Thanks. If we see increased dedicated churn during canary we roll back immediately. Keep replies short in this thread; we want an audit trail for the rollout ticket. :thumbsup:
